artifacts.description: Package entry: name, one-line purpose, canonical command, role list
Primary agent instructions: role, responsibilities, steps, output contract
Package manifest: permissions, memory policy, read allow/deny lists
Identity card: name, slug, summary, verb_object capabilities, entrypoints
Routing card: >=6 triggers (>=3 ko, >=3 en), >=4 anti-triggers (>=2 ko, >=2 en), semantic workforce block, risk profile, entrypoints, memory behavior — no card, no auto-routing
Memory ownership map
Per-runtime slash command adapters
MCP tool allowlist and resolution order
Skill registry (empty list allowed)
Append-only candidate memory events ledger (empty on export); every builder emits it and the team gate rejects a package without it
Positive/negative eval prompts with pass criteria
Interview-derived work brief: goal, constraints, decisions

>=10 routing benchmark cases (route + reject, ko + en). Canonical path is the plural `.agentlas/routing-benchmarks.jsonl`, which is what 140 of 144 forge packages and 183 live Hub releases actually ship. The contract previously said `benchmarks/`, which no generation ever wrote, so every package failed this required artifact on the path alone while the file sat on disk. The spelling carries no meaning; only agreement does.
Interview summary that grounded this package
Sources consulted during build research

Worker roster: one folder per worker at agents/<role>/agent.md, plus an orchestrator/HQ and a company-blueprint topology that names them — a team with zero workers is not a team. Verified by the same team-shape rule scripts/verify-team-package.sh runs
Team topology: orchestrator, nodes, edges
Task flow: produces/consumes graph
Governance contract seed (copied verbatim; export_only)

INPUT contract: the JSON Schema for what a requester must hand over before this method can start. Direction is carried by the filename because no package ever marked it any other way, and a schema whose direction has to be guessed from its title cannot be matched against a request. Every stated need becomes a property; `required` names the ones without which the work does not begin. Any enum reachable from matching MUST carry an escape member ("other", "unknown") - a closed list is how one stated requirement took a 3-candidate inventory to 0.

OUTPUT contract: the JSON Schema for what the requester ends up holding. The brief compiler reads only this file's TOPOLOGY - arity and value spaces - to derive shape, rowVerdict and verdictValues, so nothing here depends on the words the author chose. Extra domain schemas may sit beside it; this is the one the matcher reads.

One real instance of output.schema.json. The publish gate validates it with a JSON Schema validator, never with a model - under BYOM the only honest defence against marking your own homework is that the marker is not a model.

The compiled resume, schemaVersion agentlas.brief/1, side=offer. Written by the upload path so an author can read exactly what the routing layer sees, and NOT shipped: every field is derived from the card, the manifest and contracts/ that travel with it, so including it would tie the package's identity to the compiler — improving how a shape is inferred would mint a new release for every published package without one of them having changed. The reader compiles its own from the same sources.
